Add typed create/drop/recreate index workflows with provider-aware options.

Parent Goal: #182
Authority: `docs/goals/goal-phase-a-object-crud.md`

## Goal
Create the canonical typed schema/object mutation pipeline that all later CRUD work reuses.

## Scope
- Add canonical domain/application types such as `ObjectRef`, `ObjectAction`, `ObjectMutationRequest`, `ObjectMutationPreview`, `ObjectMutationResult`.
- Add `ObjectMutationService::plan()` and `apply()` split.
- Enforce provider capability checks server-side before SQL generation/execution.
- Reuse existing DDL builders where valid; do not duplicate SQL in UI.
- Preview must carry a fingerprint so apply rejects a request different from what was previewed.
- Route through `UiCommand`/runtime/application layers.
- Targeted schema invalidation/refresh after successful apply.
- Read-only and destructive policy integration.

## Initial object coverage
Only enough table/column mutation support to prove the framework end-to-end. Do not implement all Phase A objects here.

## Acceptance
- one typed table/column mutation can plan -> preview SQL -> confirm -> apply -> targeted refresh;
- unsupported SQLite/PostgreSQL capability fails before execution;
- UI does not construct provider SQL;
- read-only connection blocks mutation;
- destructive classification/confirmation works;
- preview fingerprint mismatch is rejected;
- focused service/runtime/UI tests.

## Merge strategy
Start from latest `main`. Merge this issue independently once accepted. Every A02+ issue must rebase/start from the merged A01 main.

Suggested commit: `feat(schema): add typed object mutation framework`
title: [Phase A][A01] Typed Object Mutation Framework

## Goal
Execute the post-v0.1 product roadmap as a sequence of small, independently mergeable issues so DB Pro grows from a strong core SQL/data/ER/Agent client into a broad database IDE.

Product direction:
- DBeaver-class database capability coverage
- Codex/VS Code-style native UX
- AI-native workflows built on canonical typed actions

Authoritative planning:
- `docs/goals/goal-full-product.md`
- `docs/goals/goal-phase-a-object-crud.md`
- `docs/goals/goal-phase-b-routines.md`
- `docs/goals/goal-phase-c-transfer.md`
- `docs/goals/goal-phase-d-monitoring.md`
- `docs/goals/goal-phase-e-security.md`
- `docs/goals/goal-phase-f-compare-migration.md`
- `docs/goals/goal-phase-g-productivity.md`
- `docs/goals/goal-phase-h-ai.md`
- `docs/notes/PRODUCT_CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md`

## Execution model
This Goal is intentionally decomposed into small mergeable issues.

For every implementation issue:
1. start from latest `main`;
2. implement only the issue scope;
3. add focused tests;
4. run affected quality gates;
5. request review with exact SHA;
6. merge accepted work to `main` immediately;
7. next issue starts from the new `main`.

Do **not** keep a mega feature branch across the full phase.

## Architecture rules
- UI -> UiCommand/Application Action -> Service -> Port -> Provider Adapter.
- No PostgreSQL/SQLite SQL construction inside renderer/view code.
- Provider capability gating is canonical and explicit.
- Destructive mutations require preview/confirmation.
- Agent reuses canonical actions; it never owns a second database implementation.
- Unsupported provider functionality is disabled/hidden with a reason, never faked.

## Workstreams
### Phase A — Database Object CRUD
Typed object mutation framework, views/materialized views, indexes, constraints, triggers, sequences, types/enums/domains, schema/database management.

### Phase B — Functions / Procedures
Routine model, explorer, source editor, create/edit/drop, typed execute/call.

### Phase C — Data Transfer
Streaming transfer foundation, CSV, Excel/JSON, export formats, progress/cancellation.

### Phase D — Monitoring / Administration
Sessions, active queries, locks, transactions, stats, size, maintenance.

### Phase E — Security
Users, roles, memberships and privilege workbench.

### Phase F — Compare / Migration
Schema snapshots/diff, dependency-aware migration preview/generation/apply.

### Phase G — Productivity / Search
Global search, command palette, saved-query organization, snippets, favorites, recent/pinned objects.

### Phase H — Advanced AI
AI workflows on top of canonical tools: optimize SQL, explain plans, analyze slow queries, migration assistance, admin assistance.

## Merge policy
Each child issue must be mergeable to `main` without requiring all sibling issues to land first. If an issue needs a foundation, express that dependency explicitly and keep the foundation small.

## Definition of done
This Goal is complete when all planned post-v0.1 milestones are either:
- Done and merged,
- intentionally Deferred with a target release,
- or superseded by a documented product decision.

No issue closes merely because code was pushed; exact acceptance evidence is required.

body:
## Status
Ready to Pick — **P1 release blocker**

Parent Goal: #14
Feeds: #122, #126, #134, #136
Baseline reviewed: `65bbca36d77f0b5720b99f59ac514b87d8fb0765`
Discovered while reviewing audit commit: `a2cf4a397cd3444ea45c3244a203f89b221a9738`

## Problem
The release claim “OS keyring + encrypted fallback” is not currently true for the production configuration.

### Source evidence
Workspace dependency:
```toml
keyring = "3"
```
No platform credential-store features are enabled.

Production bootstrap:
```rust
let vault = KeyringVault::new("com.dbpro.app", secrets_dir).with_fallback();
```

`KeyringVault` itself documents that:
- fallback is intended for development/CI;
- production should not enable it;
- fallback encryption key is derived from `service_name`, which is not secret.

Keyring v3 requires explicit credential-store features. If no supported store is enabled for a platform, its mock store is used by default. Therefore the current package configuration cannot be treated as verified OS-keyring storage.

## Risk
- production can use a development-only fallback with a predictable derivation input;
- persisted database passwords may not receive the OS-backed protection that product/docs currently claim;
- current audit conclusions about Linux `libsecret` are premature because the root dependency configuration does not select a real platform store at all;
- credentials/storage behavior across restart/platforms is not release-qualified.

Severity: **P1 / security + product-truth**.

## Required fix
1. Configure `keyring` v3 features for every supported production platform explicitly.
   - macOS: real Keychain backend;
   - Windows: Windows Credential Manager backend;
   - Linux: choose and document one persistent production backend intentionally.
2. Remove unconditional production `.with_fallback()` or replace the fallback with a production-grade design approved by #126.
3. Production must never silently use the keyring mock store.
4. Define fail-closed behavior when the OS credential store is unavailable.
5. Decide migration/cleanup behavior for existing `secrets/secrets.json` development fallback data.
6. Re-audit native/package dependencies after the Linux backend is selected; do not assume `libsecret` until the selected feature/backend proves it.
7. Update provider/platform/limitations docs so claims match the final implementation.

## Tests / evidence
- exact dependency features in Cargo metadata/lockfile;
- macOS credential survives app restart and is stored in Keychain;
- Windows credential survives restart and is stored in Credential Manager;
- Linux selected backend survives restart on supported environment;
- unavailable-store test proves fail-closed / approved fallback behavior;
- no mock store is reachable in production build;
- delete/edit lifecycle tests remain green;
- exact-head Rust tests + packaged runtime smoke for affected platforms.

## Merge gate
Do not mark release-ready while this issue is open. Any accepted fix must be reviewed on one exact SHA and reflected in #136.
title: [P1][RC1][Security] Configure real OS keyring stores and remove DEV-only fallback from production

Capabilities a credible DB IDE is expected to have and which must not be claimed as unique.

Areas where competitors establish a user expectation that our v0.1 must either meet, clearly limit, or defer honestly.

Architecture/roadmap opportunities — especially human+agent shared typed execution, capability, confirmation, cancellation and audit — clearly labeled future.

Words/category terms saturated by competitors; terms likely to create generic/confusing identity; concepts aligned with future extensibility.

- current versus future product state never blended;

## Status
In Progress — control issue

Parent Goal: #14
Related Project bootstrap: #112

## Goal
Provide one canonical queue that coding/research/review agents can inspect, claim, execute, and hand off without reading the full conversation history.

## Agent operating model
1. Open this dispatcher first.
2. Pick only a task listed under `READY TO PICK` or explicitly marked `In Progress` for your lane.
3. Read the target issue completely before editing code/docs.
4. Respect branch/PR/dependency rules in the target issue.
5. Do not broaden scope or opportunistically refactor unrelated code.
6. Before coding, comment on the target issue: `CLAIMED — <agent-id> — starting from <SHA>`.
7. During work, keep commits focused and use the suggested commit boundary unless the issue says otherwise.
8. Before handoff, comment with exact SHA, files changed, commands run, pass/fail counts, known limitations, and whether any acceptance item remains.
9. Move/report `REVIEW REQUESTED`; do not self-close implementation issues.
10. Review agent verifies exact SHA. Only accepted evidence allows issue completion.
11. Mọi implementation/review handoff phải kết thúc bằng **`Tổng kết bằng tiếng Việt`**.

## Concurrency lanes
### Lane A — Gate 4 critical path
Only one behavior-changing Gate 4 coding task at a time on `feature/er-large-schema` unless two issues explicitly state they are parallel-safe.

## Status
**In Progress — Gate 5 A2**

Parent workstream: #22
Parent gate: #21

Branch: `fix/gate5-provider-value-contract`
PR: #161
A1 accepted head: `35570b2f35cbd466785f0427e8c3ea7af9ffeff5`

## Canonical temporal semantics to lock
| PostgreSQL type | Domain/IPC semantic | Canonical string |
|---|---|---|
| DATE | calendar date, no timezone | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| TIME | wall-clock time, no timezone | `HH:MM:SS.ffffff` |
| TIMETZ | wall-clock time + explicit offset | `HH:MM:SS.ffffff±HH:MM` |
| TIMESTAMP | local date-time, **no timezone** | `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff` |
| TIMESTAMPTZ | absolute instant, normalized UTC | `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ` |

Fractional-second policy: canonical temporal values preserve PostgreSQL microsecond precision. The contract is string-based so browser/OS timezone settings never reinterpret DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP values.

## Representation plan
Dedicated semantic variants will be added for read/IPC and typed mutation plumbing:
- `date`
- `time`
- `timetz`
- `timestamp`
- `timestamptz`

Legacy `datetime` remains temporarily for existing pre-Gate-5 call sites until decoder migration #56 removes the ambiguous provider mapping.

## Mutation/editability boundary
A2 defines typed representations but does not enable temporal editing/binding. New temporal parameters must fail explicitly in provider binders until #56/#62 define provider-aware mutation policy. This prevents accidental timezone conversion or generic-text binding.

## Acceptance
- [ ] DATE semantic/string contract locked
- [ ] TIME semantic/string contract locked
- [ ] TIMETZ semantic/string contract locked
- [ ] TIMESTAMP cannot carry invented `Z`/offset
- [ ] TIMESTAMPTZ canonical UTC-instant contract locked
- [ ] fractional microseconds preserved in representative fixtures
- [ ] Tauri/frontend DTO variants mirror domain semantics
- [ ] display/copy/export return exact canonical strings
- [ ] provider binders fail explicitly for new temporal params until later workstream
- [ ] exact-head CI green
